cmocs.statement: Among novice undergraduate medical students with low domain-specific knowledge, traditional instruction delivered in a simulator setting was associated with low diagnostic accuracy.
cmocs.supporting_quote: Cardiac physical diagnosis provides a good model to test the effect of schema-based instructional guidance... multiple studies have documented poor cardiac auscultatory skills among senior medical students and residents, and resulting low rates of diagnostic success... On the practical test, schema-based instruction was associated with greater diagnostic accuracy (61% versus 26%).

cmocs.statement: For novice undergraduate medical students, schema-based instruction appeared to help learners build on what they already knew, improving structured knowledge and diagnostic accuracy.
cmocs.supporting_quote: The results on the written test provide evidence that schemas modified knowledge organisation by increasing the amount of structured knowledge without changing factual knowledge of diagnoses... Schema-based instruction was associated with higher scores on structured knowledge questions (74% versus 55%; p < 0.0001)... On the practical test, schema-based instruction was associated with greater diagnostic accuracy (61% versus 26%).

cmocs.statement: Among novice medical students, schema-based instruction was associated with greater diagnostic success for taught lesions and also for untaught lesions, consistent with more accurate non-analytical/schema-based reasoning.
cmocs.supporting_quote: Although reasoning strategy was not directly measured... schema-instructed students were more likely to report features from the schema in arriving at their diagnosis. This suggests a higher use of schema-based reasoning by schema-instructed students... Schema-based instruction was associated with greater diagnostic accuracy for both taught (77% versus 39%... p < 0.001) and untaught (44% versus 13%... p < 0.001) lesions.

cmocs.statement: Among novice undergraduate medical students, schema-based instruction improved retention of structured knowledge over 2-4 weeks.
cmocs.supporting_quote: A majority of students (n = 37, 70%) voluntarily returned for follow-up written testing 2–4 weeks later... Students in the schema group performed better on structured knowledge questions (62% versus 42%; p = 0.001)... CONCLUSIONS Schema-based instruction was associated with improved retention of structured knowledge and diagnostic performance among novices.

coder_notes: The paper clearly concerns undergraduate medical students and repeatedly frames them as novices, supporting E01 and E02. The simulator/Harvey setting supports E10 as contextually present, but the focal intervention is schema-based instruction, which has no direct Richmond intervention code; therefore intervention fields are left empty where appropriate rather than forced. Mechanisms are mostly inferred by authors rather than directly measured. I coded E39 conservatively where the paper explicitly discusses schemas modifying knowledge organisation/structured knowledge, and E24 only where authors state schema-instructed students were more likely to report schema features and suggest higher use of schema-based reasoning, noting reasoning was not directly measured. Outcomes around structured knowledge retention and diagnostic accuracy are well evidenced. No feedback, expert reasoning explanation, near-peer, or emotional/cognitive load response codes were directly evidenced in the trial results sufficiently to code.
